[Refactor] Remove MiniMax-M2 fp8 dequant load_weights patch (#13782)

## Summary
- Remove the fp8 block-dequant `load_weights` monkey-patch from
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_minimax_m2.py`.
- The patch only activates when `quantization_config.quant_method ==
"fp8"`. MiniMax-M2 W8A8 checkpoints loaded with `--quantization ascend`
never hit this path, so on NPU the patch was a no-op.
- Also drop now-unused imports (`Iterable`, `current_platform`,
`MiniMaxM2Model`, `FP8_DTYPES`) and the "fp8 load dequant" mention in
the file header.

## Why removable
`_need_dequantize_fp8_weights()` returns `False` for non-fp8 quant
configs (e.g. W8A8 via `--quantization ascend`), so
`_patched_load_weights` simply delegated to the original
`MiniMaxM2Model.load_weights` (AutoWeightsLoader). No fp8
`weight`/`weight_scale_inv` pairs exist in such checkpoints.

vllm-ascend installed from source.

baseline with the patch present.

commits.message:
[Refactor] Remove MiniMax-M2 linear attn __init__/weight_loader patches (#13800)

## Summary

- Remove the `MiniMaxText01RMSNormTP.__init__` and `weight_loader`
monkey-patches from
`vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_minimax_m2_linear_attn.py`, plus the
now-unused imports (`partial`, `nn`, `CustomOp`, TP rank/world helpers).
- The NPU q/k norm fast path (`forward_qk`) monkey-patch is **retained**
— this PR only drops the weight-sharding/init patches.

## Why removable

Both removed patches are redundant with upstream vLLM at the pinned
commit (0351e9aa,
`vllm/model_executor/layers/minimax_rms_norm/rms_norm_tp.py`):

- **`weight_loader`** is byte-for-byte identical to the upstream
`@staticmethod MiniMaxText01RMSNormTP.weight_loader`
(rms_norm_tp.py:336-350): same `loaded_weight.shape[0] //
shard_world_size` slice-and-copy.
- **`__init__`** differs from upstream only by (a) an extra `hidden_size
% weight_shard_world` divisibility check and (b) skipping the Lamport
fused-allreduce workspace setup. On NPU the workspace setup is a no-op:
it is gated by `_MINIMAX_FUSED_AR_RMS_QK =
torch.ops._C.minimax_allreduce_rms_qk` (a CUDA csrc op, `None` on NPU
builds), and even if reached it is wrapped in try/except with the
`lamport_workspace` module importing `cuda` bindings. Weight-sharding
semantics are identical to upstream.

The retained `forward_qk` patch is unaffected: it does not reference the
removed helpers, and the linear-attention path uses
`MiniMaxText01RMSNormTP._forward` (untouched) plus this NPU q/k fast
path.

## Test plan

- Environment: Atlas 800I A2 (A3), CANN 9.1.0 snapshot, vllm +
vllm-ascend from source.
- Model: `/mnt/weight/MiniMax-M2.7-w8a8-QuaRot`, TP8, `--quantization
ascend`, EP enabled.
- With the patches removed: `vllm serve` starts cleanly (`Application
startup complete`, no errors), chat-completion smoke returns correct
output (`2+2 -> 4`, `finish_reason=stop`).

- vLLM version: v0.26.0
- vLLM main:
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/58d3918e3ea0a544ffedadad2ba84559e9c51d8f

commits.message:
[Refactor][SFA] Remove unused SFA state and redundant branches (#14097)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR removes dead state and redundant control flow from the Ascend
SFA implementation:

- removes unused metadata-builder state (`block_size`, `max_blocks`, and
`rope_dim`);
- stops retaining unused implementation attributes while preserving the
`MLAAttentionImpl` constructor contract;
- avoids the unused tensor-parallel rank lookup and moves the type-only
`NPUInputBatch` import behind `TYPE_CHECKING`;
- simplifies KV-cache branches after the composed cache has already been
asserted non-null;
- replaces the unreachable nullable LI C8 scale branch with an explicit
invariant assertion;
- removes the redundant output alias and returns the result of
`_finalize_o_proj` directly;
- updates SFA unit tests to remove the obsolete TP-rank mock and verify
that `forward` propagates the finalized output.

These changes reduce stale state and make the existing SFA invariants
and output contract explicit without changing the attention computation.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. This is an internal refactor with no API, configuration, or
inference behavior change.

### How was this patch tested?

- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- `python -m py_compile vllm_ascend/attention/sfa_v1.py
tests/ut/attention/a2/test_sfa_v1.py
tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_o_proj_tp.py`

The NPU-dependent unit tests were not run locally because this workspace
requires an Ascend remote container for `torch_npu` execution. The
affected UT was updated to cover `_finalize_o_proj` return-value
propagation.

commits.comment: Bugfix/feature for MRV2 spec decode. (1) Implements real probabilistic rejection sampling: the previous _probabilistic_rejection_kernel always accepted draft tokens (u=0.0) because NPU Triton lacks float64 tl_rand64 and scalar tl.rand; the rewrite draws u from a 1-element block with tl.randint/tl.rand and clamps it away from 0 so tl.log stays finite. (2) Fixes DFlash/DSpark full-graph padding: when a draft batch is padded to a cudagraph capture size, upstream _build_draft_attn_metadata clamps query_start_loc to the real request count, violating the Ascend FIA TND invariant (last(actual_seq_lengths_q) == query token count); the new _update_draft_attn_metadata rebuilds actual_seq_lengths_q from the padded count, mirroring Eagle. (3) Also rewrites the gumbel sampling kernel from a 2D grid to a per-token 1D grid with an internal num_blocks loop, adds per-token processed_logits_col support, and broadens the triton gumbel_sample patch to base_speculator/gumbel modules. This changes actual sampling behavior (acceptance rate no longer 1.0) and the kernel rewrite is performance-sensitive; no automated tests were added in this PR (validated via example scripts).

test_impact.reason: probabilistic rejection sampling 行为有实质变更（接受率从恒 1.0 变为真实随机），且 gumbel kernel 从 2D grid 改为 1D grid + num_blocks 循环，属于采样正确性与性能敏感路径；提交未新增任何 UT，建议补充 rejection sampler 与 gumbel kernel 的单元测试，以及 DFlash/DSpark 的 full-graph padding 回归测试。

commits.message:
[Bugfix][MRV2] Support probabilistic rejection sampling for spec decode (#13470)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
1. Enables probabilistic rejection sampling
(`draft_sample_method="probabilistic"`) for DFlash/DSpark speculative
decoding.

2. Previously `_probabilistic_rejection_kernel` always accepted every
draft token (`u = 0.0`) because NPU Triton lacks float64 `tl_rand64` and
scalar `tl.rand`, which made the reported acceptance rate 1.0. This PR
implements the real acceptance test.

3. Fix the full graph for DFlash: Draft batches padded to the next
cudagraph capture size (num_reqs_padded >
num_reqs) leave actual_seq_lengths_q short of the replayed graph's token
count, because upstream `Speculator._build_draft_attn_metadata` clamps`
query_start_loc` at the real request count. The Ascend FIA TND check
(`queryT == last element of actualSequenceLengthQ`) then fails and the
engine aborts (e.g. 55 requests on gsm8k: 495 padded to 504).

commits.message:
[Refactor][Distributed] Remove all_to_all patch and switch lm-head TP to all_to_all_single (#12923)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Removes the `GroupCoordinator.all_to_all` monkey-patch from vllm-ascend
and switches all remaining consumers to a new `lmhead_all_to_all` helper
that uses `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single`, returning to the
upstream PyTorch standard interface.

This is a re-opening of #11086.

**Background** — the old path required two layers of patch:
```
consumer → get_lmhead_tp_group().all_to_all()   ← GroupCoordinatorPatch.all_to_all
         → device_communicator.all_to_all()      ← NPUCommunicator.all_to_all
         → dist.all_to_all(list version)          ← real HCCL call
```

**Changes:**
- Delete `GroupCoordinatorPatch.all_to_all` and
`NPUCommunicator.all_to_all` (preserving `_NpuAll2AllManager`).
- Add `lmhead_all_to_all(logits, comm_group)` helper in
`vocab_parallel_embedding.py`, used by all 4 consumers:
  - `vocab_parallel_embedding.py:_get_logits_lmheadtp`
- `spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:_run_merged_draft` (2 sites,
reduce_sample branches)
  - `spec_decode/step3p5.py:_sample_draft_tokens_for_step` (Step3.5 MTP)

**The redistribution `[N, V/P] → [N/P, V]`** (all tokens × partial vocab
→ partial tokens × full vocab) is done with a `view + all_to_all_single
+ permute + view` sequence:
```
[N, V/P] -> view(P, N/P, V/P) -> all_to_all_single -> permute(1,0,2) -> view(N/P, V)
```
This is mathematically equivalent to the removed patch's
`tensor_split(dim=0) + all_to_all(list) + cat(dim=-1)`, but keeps a
single contiguous buffer for better HCCL fusion. Microbenchmarks on
Ascend 910 (P=2/4, realistic lm-head shapes) show **1.2x–1.4x speedup**
over the list version.

**Why not a bare `all_to_all_single`?** A naive `all_to_all_single` only
redistributes on dim 0 (token) and never gathers the vocab dimension —
it silently produces `[N, V/P]` instead of `[N/P, V]`. The `view`
reshapes the input so dim 0 carries the per-rank token shard, letting
the single collective route correctly; `permute` then interleaves the
vocab shards of each token.

**Safety:** equal split is guaranteed because `pad_vocab_size` +
`divide` make the vocab shard `V/P` identical on every rank. `world_size
== 1` returns the input unchanged. For the dynamic token axis,
`lmhead_all_to_all` raises a clear `ValueError` when `N` is not
divisible by `world_size`; on the live lm-head path this is structural —
`N` comes from `all_gather(hidden_states, dim=0)`, so `N = world_size ×
N_local` by construction. The three spec-decode call sites are defensive
only: `enable_reduce_sample` and lm-head TP are mutually exclusive at
startup (`ascend_config.py` raises `ValueError`), so those branches are
unreachable today and need no round-up padding.

**Alignment with project direction:** the patch registration comment in
`patch/__init__.py` already notes "Remove this patch when the refactor
of all2all manager is done." This PR takes a step in that direction by
removing the upper `GroupCoordinator` patch and using
`dist.all_to_all_single` directly — the same pattern already used in
`dsa_v1.py`, `dsa_cp.py`, `sfa_cp.py`, etc.

Also removes the patch registration comment block in `patch/__init__.py`
and cleans up 4 affected test files.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No. The behavior of lm-head tensor parallel is unchanged; the refactor
only replaces the internal communication call with an equivalent (and
faster) one. No API, config, or model interface changes.

### How was this patch tested?

- **Lint:** `ruff check vllm_ascend/` clean, `ruff format --check` clean
on all modified files.
- **Correctness simulation (4-rank, CPU):** verified the view-based
helper is bit-identical to the removed list-based `tensor_split +
all_to_all(list) + cat` implementation for P=4 / N=16 / V=8.
- **Unit tests (Ascend NPU, CI):** the `a2-1` selected-tests group
covers the modified UT files (`test_vocab_parallel_embedding.py`,
`test_patch_distributed.py`, `test_lmhead_all_to_all.py`) plus the
Step3.5 MTP e2e.
- **Correctness microbench (2-rank gloo + 2/4-rank HCCL):** verified
element-wise identical output to the old list-based version.
- **Performance microbench (Ascend 910, HCCL):** view version is
1.2x–1.4x faster than the list version.
- **E2E, graph mode (Atlas A3, Qwen3-30B-A3B-W8A8, TP1×DP8 +
lmhead_tp=4):** conversation checks (Chinese / English / math / code
generation) all coherent, Qwen3 thinking behavior normal. A/B benchmark
on identical config (random dataset, in=1024 / out=256, 64 prompts, 5
rounds each; the only difference is the vllm-ascend commit — PR
`2c888b4d2` vs main @ merge-base `e80067d46`):

  | Metric | PR | baseline | Δ (5 rounds / warm-state) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | TPOT | 44.30 ms | 45.91 ms | **-3.5% / -2.2%** |
  | Request throughput | 4.95 req/s | 4.80 req/s | **+3.1% / +2.4%** |
| Output throughput | 1267.5 tok/s | 1228.9 tok/s | **+3.1% / +2.4%** |
  | Mean TTFT | 1381.6 ms | 1381.4 ms | flat (prefill untouched) |

  (warm-state = rounds 2–5, excluding the cold-start round)
